The last code change was 1f761131fa83f5ed3cd6f2f22b225c4501d154fa (2026-07-06, modeling_minicpmo.py #18). License is apache-2.0 and the repo is not gated. It has 54 files totalling 20,048,635,793 bytes (20.05 GB / 18.67 GiB). That breaks down as: 4 bf16 safetensors shards, 18.744 GB (9,371,787,666 params; modules llm/vpm/apm/tts/resampler/audio_projection_layer); assets/token2wav vocoder, 1.231 GB, which streaming/TTS needs; about 57 MB of demo media that inference does not need; and custom trust_remote_code files (configuration_minicpmo.py, modeling_minicpmo.py, modeling_navit_siglip.py, processing_minicpmo.py, tokenization_minicpmo_fast.py, utils.py). There are no separate TTS sub-repos: the vocoder (CosyVoice2-style flow + HiFT + s3 speech tokenizer + campplus) is in assets/token2wav. Its Python code comes from the pip package minicpmo-utils[all], which provides the stepaudio2, s3tokenizer and minicpmo modules. Card pins: transformers==4.51.0, torch>=2.3.0,<=2.8.0, torchaudio<=2.8.0, minicpmo-utils[all]>=1.0.5,<=1.0.6, plus accelerate; tested on Python 3.10; ffmpeg for video. flash-attn is optional (attn_implementation 'sdpa' or 'flash_attention_2'). Streaming: full-duplex via model.as_duplex() -> MiniCPMODuplex, then .prepare(...) and a loop of .streaming_prefill(audio_waveform=1s 16kHz chunk, frame_list=[PIL frame]) + .streaming_generate(...) that returns is_listen/text/audio_waveform (24 kHz). Half-duplex streaming via MiniCPMO.streaming_prefill(session_id, msgs, omni_mode, is_last_chunk) + streaming_generate(session_id, generate_audio...). Offline: model.chat(msgs, omni_mode=True, generate_audio=True...). Memory: the card's efficiency table gives 19.0 GB (bf16) and 11.0 GB (int4) GPU memory, with no GPU named. The PyTorch realtime web demo needs an NVIDIA GPU with at least 28 GB; its repo states ~21.5 GB VRAM per worker. llama.cpp-omni needs at least 12 GB on an NVIDIA GPU. Official quantized repos: openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5-awq (13.07 GB, older custom code), openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5-GPTQ (9.77 GB, W4A16, ~11 GB documented), and openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5-gguf (79.97 GB for all files; Q4_K_M LLM 5.03 GB plus audio/vision/tts/token2wav GGUFs). Deployment gotchas: (1) init_tts() downloads assets/token2wav from repo_id "openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5" with snapshot_download and no revision pin, unless model_dir or a local model path is used. (2) MiniCPMODuplex.from_existing_model loads AutoTokenizer/Processor by name_or_path without a revision. (3) Token2wav hard-codes .cuda() and runs campplus on onnxruntime CPUExecutionProvider. (4) minicpmo-utils 1.0.5–1.0.7 pins librosa==0.9.0, while the demo repo's requirements say librosa>=0.10.2 because 0.9.x breaks under newer setuptools.

MiniCPMO.init_tts(model_dir=None, enable_float16=False, n_timesteps=10) does `from stepaudio2 import Token2wav`, raising 'Please install Token2wav via: pip install minicpmo-utils[all]' if it is missing. It then calls _ensure_asset_dir('assets/token2wav'). If os.path.join(config._name_or_path, 'assets/token2wav') does not exist locally, that function runs huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(repo_id="openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5", allow_patterns=["assets/token2wav/**"]) WITHOUT a revision pin. For a reproducible deploy, load from a local snapshot directory or pass model_dir.

In minicpmo-utils 1.0.6, stepaudio2/token2wav.py Token2wav(model_path, float16=False, n_timesteps=10) loads speech_tokenizer_v2_25hz.onnx via s3tokenizer.load_model(...).cuda(). It runs campplus.onnx with onnxruntime providers=['CPUExecutionProvider'], loads flow.yaml via load_hyperpyyaml (registering cosyvoice2.* aliases to stepaudio2.cosyvoice2), and moves flow.pt/hift.pt to .cuda(). It hard-codes CUDA. The sdist minicpmo_utils-1.0.6.tar.gz (292,148 B, sha256 3b35de45a46db449079d96fc96723df4151ab8db319888016edfd9475f9406c3) contains the packages minicpmo, stepaudio2 (with cosyvoice2, flashcosyvoice) and s3tokenizer.

Card-documented modes: (1) Duplex Omni Mode, full-duplex streaming for real-time video+audio. (2) Half-Duplex Omni Mode, via chat (model.chat(msgs, omni_mode=True, generate_audio=True, output_audio_path=..., use_tts_template=True, max_slice_nums=1)) or streaming (streaming_prefill/streaming_generate). (3) Half-Duplex Realtime Speech Conversation (audio-only, 1 s chunks). (4) Speech/Audio Mode: zero-shot TTS, mimick, ASR/audio understanding. (5) Visual understanding: single image, multi-image, few-shot, video via get_video_frame_audio_segments. Also enable_thinking True/False (instruct and thinking in one model) and OpenAI-style structured content (image_url / audio_url / video_url with use_audio and stack_frames).

AutoModel.from_pretrained("openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5", trust_remote_code=True, attn_implementation="sdpa", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, init_vision=True, init_audio=True, init_tts=True); model.eval().cuda(); model.init_tts(); duplex_model = model.as_duplex(); model = duplex_model.as_simplex(reset_session=True). Vision-only: init_audio=False, init_tts=False. Audio-only: init_vision=False.

model.as_duplex(device=None, **kwargs) returns MiniCPMODuplex (class in modeling_minicpmo.py), which calls model.init_tts internally. Default duplex params include generate_audio True, ls_mode 'explicit', max_new_speak_tokens_per_chunk 20, temperature 0.7, top_k 100, top_p 0.8, chunk_ms 1000, first_chunk_ms 1035, sample_rate 16000, sliding_window_mode 'off' (options off/basic/context; basic watermarks 8000/6000 tokens; context_max_units 24). Usage: duplex.prepare(prefix_system_prompt="Streaming Omni Conversation.", ref_audio=<16 kHz np array>, prompt_wav_path=<wav>). Then per 1 s chunk: duplex.streaming_prefill(audio_waveform=chunk, frame_list=[frame(, stacked_frame)], max_slice_nums=1, batch_vision_feed=False), followed by result = duplex.streaming_generate(prompt_wav_path=..., max_new_speak_tokens_per_chunk=20, decode_mode="sampling"). The result dict has is_listen, text, end_of_turn, current_time, audio_waveform (24 kHz output; output_sample_rate=24000) and cost_* timings. Control methods: set_break_event, set_session_stop, get_generated_text, as_simplex(reset_session=True, reset_token2wav_cache=False).

MiniCPMO.streaming_prefill(session_id, msgs, omni_mode=True, max_slice_nums=None, use_tts_template=True, enable_thinking=False, is_last_chunk=False, ...) and MiniCPMO.streaming_generate(session_id, generate_audio=True, audio_token_chunk_size=25, max_new_tokens=256, enable_thinking=False, use_tts_template=True, do_sample=True, ...). The generator yields (wav_chunk, text_chunk) when generate_audio is set, otherwise (text_chunk, is_finished). Also reset_session(reset_token2wav_cache=True), init_token2wav_cache(prompt_speech_16k=ref_audio), and get_sys_prompt(ref_audio=..., mode="omni", language="en"). Input audio is 16 kHz in 1 s chunks (last chunk padded to 16000 samples); output is 24 kHz. For realtime speech the card suggests length_penalty=1.1.

from minicpmo.utils import get_video_frame_audio_segments, generate_duplex_video (in the minicpmo-utils package). Signature: get_video_frame_audio_segments(video_path, audio_path=None, last_vad_timestamp=None, stack_frames=1, use_ffmpeg=False, adjust_audio_length=False, use_audio=True), returning (video_frames: List[PIL.Image], audio_segments: List[np.ndarray] or None, stacked_frames or None). It extracts at 1 fps (10 fps then uniform sampling for long videos). The card says 'Use stack_frames=5 for high refresh rate mode' and claims video support 'up to 10fps'.

summary:
I read OpenBMB/MiniCPM-o-Demo on its default branch `main`. HEAD is 47709a9210dfd71afa76c058e017fc8c4db5c8d2, committed 2026-09-15T07:16:25Z ("Merge pull request #67 ... fix/speaker-sink-at-session-start"). I fetched the tree, READMEs, all 3 Dockerfiles, both entrypoints, all 6 compose files, requirements.txt, install.sh, config.example.json, config.py, gateway.py, worker.py, py_backend/server.py, the backend factory and processors, the deployment/compile/attention/realtime-API docs and the omni frontend JS. I also checked llama.cpp-omni at master a64932ec615e1463158129feaf2f0752d0c07a2e, the Hugging Face model APIs and PyPI minicpmo-utils.

ARCHITECTURE. The request path is Browser -> Gateway -> Python Worker -> Backend.
- **Gateway** (gateway.py, no torch, does not load the model) is the only public process. It serves HTTPS/WSS on :8006 with a self-signed TLS cert by default, or plain HTTP with `--http`. In the same process it runs a second plain-HTTP server on :8007 for worker registration. It handles queueing, session recording and worker health polling every 10 s.
- **Worker** (worker.py, :22400) only forwards traffic. It exposes WS /v1/worker/chat, WS /v1/worker/duplex and GET /health, and forwards to the backend given by `--backend-server-url`.
- **Backend** (:22500, bound to localhost inside the container) loads the model. It exposes WS /backend, POST /sessions/{id}/close and GET /health. It is either `python -m py_backend.server` (PyTorch/transformers) or `llama-omni-server` (C++, from tc-mb/llama.cpp-omni, GGUF).
- **Transport** is WebSocket only, with JSON text frames; there is no WebRTC. Clients connect to `wss://host/v1/realtime?mode={chat|video|audio}`.
  - Input audio is base64 float32 PCM, 16 kHz mono, about 1 s per chunk. Video is base64 JPEG in `input.video_frames`. The browser sends 1 frame per second at JPEG quality 0.7.
  - Output audio is 24 kHz float32 PCM.
  - Video sessions are capped at 300 s and audio sessions at 600 s by the gateway.
- **Concurrency**: each backend allows one active session ("backend already has an active session"), so it is one concurrent duplex session per GPU worker. Other users queue at the gateway (max_queue_size 1000).

BACKENDS. There are two: PyTorch and C++ llama.cpp-omni. Both implement full_duplex video+audio. The PyTorch one is described as the lossless reference ("100% precision"). The C++ server uses only the first frame of each input.append. vLLM and SGLang are mentioned only as "future" adapters and are not implemented.

PINS AND IMAGES.
- requirements.txt: transformers==4.51.0, accelerate==1.12.0, minicpmo-utils[all]>=1.0.5. PyPI latest is 1.0.7, uploaded 2026-10-16, and it pins librosa==0.9.0, which conflicts with requirements' librosa>=0.10.2. Also fastapi>=0.128.0, uvicorn>=0.40.0, websockets>=16.0, pydantic>=2.11.0, numpy>=2.2.0, among others.
- Worker image: python:3.12-slim-bookworm plus torch==2.8.0 and torchaudio==2.8.0 from the cu128 index (CUDA 12.8 is bundled in the wheel).
- Gateway image: oven/bun:1-slim builders, then python:3.12-slim-bookworm.
- C++ image: nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 to build, nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 to run. It builds llama.cpp-omni at unpinned origin/master with `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80;120`.
- The docs and install.sh say Python 3.10; the Docker images use 3.12.

CUDA EXTENSIONS AND COMPILE. No CUDA extension is built in the PyTorch image. flash-attn is not installed (its install.sh step is commented out), and attn "auto" falls back to sdpa. torch.compile is off by default and can only be turned on through config.json `service.compile: true`. Turned on, it adds about 15 min the first time and about 5 min on later starts that reuse the cache; the cache is TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/app/torch_compile_cache. The C++ image compiles with nvcc.

MODEL LOADING. The model path comes from `--model-path` or config `model.model_path`; the example config default is the HF id openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5, which the docs say auto-downloads. Docker mounts weights read-only at /models/MiniCPM-o-4_5 and exits if that directory is missing, so the main weights are never downloaded there. However, if `<model_path>/assets/token2wav` is missing, startup calls `snapshot_download(repo_id="openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5", allow_patterns=["assets/token2wav/**"])`. The HF repo (sha d59117d1..., 20.05 GB) contains that folder.

HEALTH. backend GET :22500/health returns status "ready". worker GET :22400/health always reports model_loaded true when forwarding, so the entrypoint waits on the backend's /health instead, for up to 600 s. gateway has GET :8006/health, /status and /workers, plus internal GET :8007/health. The Docker healthcheck curls the worker's /health (interval 15s, retries 40, start_period 120s).

SHUTDOWN. The entrypoint traps SIGTERM/SIGINT, kills the worker and then the backend, and the container exits if either child dies. The backend lifespan closes active sessions with reason "server_shutdown". Commands are `docker compose down` or, per the docs, `pkill -f "gateway.py|worker.py"` (that pattern does not match the `py_backend.server` process).

TLS AND AUTH. There is no authentication on /v1/realtime or on the internal :8007 registration API. Only admin routes are hidden, unless ENABLE_PUBLIC_ADMIN is set. The repo commits a self-signed cert and key under certs/ (CN=minicpmo45-dev, valid until 2027-02-11).

GPU MEMORY AND 24 GB GPUs.
- The README requires an NVIDIA GPU with more than 28 GB of VRAM; usage is about 21.5 GB per worker after initialization (21.8 GB in the multi-worker compose file).
- compile.md says an RTX 4090 (like an A100) takes about 0.9 s per 1-second unit in Omni Full-Duplex, which "approach[es] the 1-second real-time threshold and caus[es] noticeable stuttering". torch.compile brings this to about 0.5 s (A100 figure).
- RTX 3090 is not mentioned anywhere in the demo repo.
- llama.cpp-omni lists Full Omni VRAM at about 20 GB (F16), 13 GB (Q8_0) and 9 GB (Q4_K_M), and an RTX 4090 F16 time to first token under 550 ms.

DOC DRIFT. docs/en/deployment.md and compile.md refer to `start_all.sh` and `worker.py --compile`, but neither exists at main HEAD. The documented manual worker command lacks `--backend-server-url`, so that worker would not serve sessions.

PRICES. The repo has no prices.

HEAD SHA is 47709a9210dfd71afa76c058e017fc8c4db5c8d2, committed 2026-09-15T07:16:25Z with message 'Merge pull request #67 from AlessandroBonomo28/fix/speaker-sink-at-session-start'. Other branches: Comni at 9af4308a93ca889ddf5c7c7bde1bcfbb6ff9b147 (2026-05-11, a C++/llama.cpp-omni oriented demo that the llama.cpp-omni README recommends), awq at b11502ef09c952a527847cb3db235d6d37ef0685 (0 commits ahead and 304 behind main, i.e. already merged), and realtime-protocol, feat/omni-ws-client, o45-fc and others.

The README diagram is Frontend -(HTTPS/WSS)-> Gateway (:8006, HTTPS) -(HTTP/WS internal)-> Worker Pool (:22400+). Three runtime roles are named: 'Browser -> Gateway -> Python Worker -> Backend'. The Gateway 'does not load the model'. The Backend is either py_backend/server.py (PyTorch) or llama-omni-server (llama.cpp-omni).

Ports are: gateway public :8006 (HTTPS by default); gateway internal registry :8007 (plain HTTP, `expose` only in compose, not published); worker :22400 (bound 0.0.0.0 in the container, reached by the gateway over the compose network); backend :22500 (`EXPOSE`d in the worker-backend Dockerfile but not published by compose; the worker reaches it via 127.0.0.1). Compose publishes only "${GATEWAY_HOST_PORT:-8006}:8006".

gateway.py main() runs two uvicorn servers in one process with asyncio.gather. The public FastAPI app listens on --port (default config gateway_port 8006) with ssl_certfile/ssl_keyfile when HTTPS and ws_max_size=128 MiB. internal_app listens on --internal-port (default 8007) over plain HTTP. CLI args: --port, --internal-port 8007, --host 0.0.0.0, --max-queue-size, --timeout, --https (default True) / --http, --ssl-certfile certs/cert.pem, --ssl-keyfile certs/key.pem, --lang zh|en.

The only public WebSocket is `/v1/realtime?mode=` with mode = chat, video or audio (default video). mode=video maps to request_type omni_duplex with max_duration_s=300. mode=audio maps to audio_duplex with 600 s. mode=chat maps to the worker path /v1/worker/chat. The gateway proxies to the worker at ws://{worker.host}:{worker.port}/v1/worker/duplex (plain ws, max_size 128 MiB). On timeout it sends {"type":"session.closed","reason":"timeout"}.

Messages are JSON text frames. Lifecycle: session.queued/session.queue_update (optional), then session.queue_done, then client session.init {payload:{system_prompt|instructions, config, voice.ref_audio_base64, voice.tts_ref_audio_base64}}, then session.created, then input.append {input:{audio, video_frames[], force_listen, max_slice_nums}}, then response.output.delta with kind listen, text or audio, then session.close, then session.closed. Input audio is 16 kHz mono float32 PCM in base64. Video frames are base64 JPEG. Output audio is 24 kHz mono float32 PCM in base64. Video full-duplex has a 300 second total session limit. There is no WebRTC.

static/omni/omni-app.js uses SAMPLE_RATE_IN = 16000, SAMPLE_RATE_OUT = 24000 and CHUNK_MS = 1000. It captures one frame per chunk with canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.7) at the camera's native resolution; a code comment says the backend scales with scale_resolution=448. It connects to `${proto}://${location.host}/v1/realtime?mode=video` and errors without HTTPS ('浏览器不支持 getUserMedia，请使用 HTTPS 访问', i.e. the browser does not support getUserMedia, please use HTTPS).

The backend allows one active session: BackendServerState.register raises 'backend already has an active session'. The worker closes a new WS with 1013 'Worker busy' if it is not idle. That makes one concurrent session per worker/GPU; extra clients queue at the gateway (config max_queue_size 1000, request_timeout 300.0).

Workers register dynamically: `PUT http://gateway:8007/internal/workers/{worker_id}` with JSON {"endpoint":"host:port","gpu_group":"..."}. The endpoint must be host:port with no scheme. There is no authentication. The gateway polls each worker's GET /health every HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL = 10.0 s with a 5.0 s timeout.

Quick start: `mkdir -p certs data; openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 365 -keyout certs/key.pem -out certs/cert.pem -subj "/CN=minicpm-o"; MODEL_HOST_PATH=/path/to/MiniCPM-o-4_5 docker compose up -d --build`. docker-compose.yml defines worker-backend-0 (device_ids ["0"]) and worker-backend-1 (device_ids ["1"]), both image minicpm-wb:dev, so 2 GPUs are assumed and the file must be edited for 1 GPU. Mounts: ${MODEL_HOST_PATH}:/models/MiniCPM-o-4_5:ro, gateway ${DATA_HOST_PATH:-./data}:/app/data and ${CERTS_HOST_PATH:-./certs}:/app/certs:ro. Gateway command: --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8006 --internal-port 8007 --https --ssl-certfile /app/certs/cert.pem --ssl-keyfile /app/certs/key.pem. restart: unless-stopped.

docker/entrypoint-worker-backend.sh env vars: MODEL_PATH (default /models/MiniCPM-o-4_5), BACKEND_PORT 22500, WORKER_PORT 22400, GPU_ID 0, GATEWAY_REGISTRY_URL, WORKER_ID (default hostname), WORKER_ENDPOINT, WORKER_GPU_GROUP. Steps: (1) copy config.example.json to config.json if missing; (2) exit 1 if the MODEL_PATH dir is missing; (3) run `python -m py_backend.server --host 0.0.0.0 --port $BACKEND_PORT --gpu-id $GPU_ID --model-path $MODEL_PATH &`; (4) poll http://127.0.0.1:22500/health every 2 s for up to 300 tries (600 s); (5) run `python worker.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port $WORKER_PORT --gpu-id $GPU_ID --backend-server-url http://127.0.0.1:$BACKEND_PORT &`; (6) curl PUT registration, up to 60 tries x 2 s; (7) check every 5 s and exit the container if either child dies.

The entrypoint runs `trap cleanup SIGTERM SIGINT`; cleanup kills the worker pid and then the backend pid, runs `wait` and exits 0. The py_backend lifespan closes every session with reason 'server_shutdown' and calls backend.shutdown(), which is a no-op for PyTorch. The gateway lifespan cancels the cleanup task and calls worker_pool.stop(). README stop commands: `docker compose down` and `docker compose -f docker-compose.cpp.yml down`. The docs give a bare-metal stop of `pkill -f "gateway.py|worker.py"`; that pattern does not match `python -m py_backend.server` (my reading).

Reference bare-metal order is backend, then worker, then gateway, each with PYTHONPATH=.: `python -m py_backend.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 22500 --gpu-id 0 --model-path <dir>`; `python worker.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 22400 --gpu-id 0 --backend-server-url http://127.0.0.1:22500`; `python gateway.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8006 --internal-port 8007 --http`; then `curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8007/internal/workers/local-worker -H 'content-type: application/json' --data '{"endpoint":"127.0.0.1:22400","gpu_group":"gpu-0"}'`. End-to-end test: tests/e2e_realtime.py.

docs/en/deployment.md and docs/en/compile.md refer to `start_all.sh` and `worker.py ... --compile`. start_all.sh is not in the main tree at 47709a9 (install.sh also prints 'bash start_all.sh'), and worker.py argparse has no --compile option. A worker started without --backend-server-url loads the model in-process, but its /v1/worker/* WS endpoints close with 1013 'Backend server URL is not configured', so the documented 'Manual Start' worker command would not serve sessions.

config.example.json contains: model.model_path "openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5", pt_path null, attn_implementation "auto"; audio.ref_audio_path "assets/ref_audio/ref_minicpm_signature.wav", playback_delay_ms 200, chat_vocoder "token2wav"; service.gateway_port 8006, worker_base_port 22400, max_queue_size 1000, request_timeout 300.0, compile false, data_dir "data"; duplex.pause_timeout 60.0. Backend: GET :22500/health returns {status:'ready' or 'loading', backend:'pytorch', worker_status, active_session_id}. It is served only after the lifespan model load completes. Worker: GET :22400/health returns WorkerHealthResponse {status, worker_status, gpu_id, model_loaded, current_ticket_id, total_requests, avg_inference_time_ms, kv_cache_length, capabilities[chat, streaming, half_duplex_audio, audio_duplex, omni_duplex]}. In forwarding mode model_loaded is always true, so the entrypoint gates on the backend's /health instead. Gateway: GET :8006/health returns {status:'healthy', timestamp}; also GET /status and GET /workers, and internal GET :8007/health. The gateway defaults to HTTPS (--https default True) with --ssl-certfile certs/cert.pem and --ssl-keyfile certs/key.pem. If either file is missing it logs an error and returns, i.e. it does not start. `--http` disables TLS with the warning 'Browser microphone/camera APIs may not work.' The repo commits a self-signed certs/cert.pem (CN=minicpmo45-dev, valid Feb 11 2026 to Feb 11 2027) and certs/key.pem; .dockerignore excludes certs/, so compose mounts ./certs read-only. Worker and backend traffic is plain ws/http.

There is no authentication or API key on /v1/realtime or the other public gateway routes, and no CORS middleware. Admin surfaces (/admin, /api/admin/*, /static/admin.html) return 404 unless the ENABLE_PUBLIC_ADMIN env var is 1, true, yes or on. The internal registry PUT /internal/workers/{id} on :8007 is unauthenticated.

The current main commit is dfe5db0cabf054c4615c796306a51f9b0ee399ca (2026-10-16T15:13:55Z, "docs: add homepage model weights and explicit DSpark format links"). Its weights are 4 safetensors shards totalling about 18.7 GB, and the whole repo is 20.05 GB including token2wav assets.

OFFICIAL WAYS TO RUN STREAMING OMNI (video + audio in, speech out). Only two paths are documented.
(A) PyTorch + HF Transformers. This is the "recommended, 100% precision" path. It uses model.as_duplex(), then prepare, streaming_prefill and streaming_generate. The officially recommended server is OpenBMB/MiniCPM-o-Demo (the old URL minicpm-o-4_5-pytorch-simple-demo redirects there), main 47709a9210dfd71afa76c058e017fc8c4db5c8d2. It supports omni full-duplex, audio full-duplex and turn-based chat. Its stated requirement is an NVIDIA GPU with more than 28 GB and Linux. Measured VRAM is about 21.5 GB per worker. Omni duplex takes about 0.9 s per 1 s unit on A100 or RTX 4090, close to real time; torch.compile brings that to about 0.5 s on A100.
(B) llama.cpp-omni, a C++ engine running the GGUF files. It supports half-duplex speech and full-duplex omni streaming. Requirements: an NVIDIA GPU with at least 12 GB, or for full-duplex on a Mac, an M4 Max with at least 24 GB. It serves llama-omni-server on WebSocket /backend with full_duplex mode, 1 s audio plus video frames per input.append and speak/listen decided at 1 Hz. VRAM for the full omni set: Q4_K_M about 9 GB, Q8_0 about 13 GB, F16 about 20 GB. Speed on RTX 4090 F16: first token under 550 ms, Token2Wav RTF about 0.15x. The cookbook's commands were verified on an RTX 4090. The MiniCPM-o-Demo repo can also use this C++ engine as its backend (docker-compose.cpp.yml, defaulting to MiniCPM-o-4_5-Q4_K_M.gguf with -c 8192).

TEXT OUTPUT ONLY (no speech, no duplex) in the official guides:
- vLLM: support was upstreamed in PR #33431 (merged 2026-02-06) and ships in vllm>=0.16.0. The guide shows image, video and audio input with text output.
- SGLang: the cookbook guide shows image input with text output only. Upstream SGLang PR #18420 ("Support MiniCPM-o 4.5") was closed without merging. Upstream minicpmo.py imports only Qwen2ForCausalLM (no Qwen3), so upstream support for 4.5 is UNCONFIRMED.
- Mainline llama.cpp: llama-mtmd-cli with image input only.
- Ollama: openbmb/minicpm-o4.5, image input only, via the tc-mb/ollama fork on branch MiniCPM-V.
- AWQ guide: vLLM or AutoAWQ (tc-mb fork), image examples only.

24 GB GPU. The officially documented configuration that fits 24 GB and supports full-duplex video + audio with speech out is llama.cpp-omni plus openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5-gguf. The WebRTC_Demo README marks RTX 4090 24GB and RTX 3090 24GB as duplex ✅, and says the full Q4_K_M set is about 8.3 GB on disk and about 10 GB at runtime. One build gotcha: the Demo's Dockerfile.cpp-worker-backend defaults to CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80;120, which leaves out sm_89 (RTX 40 series). The cookbook says to add 89 and rebuild. The PyTorch BF16 path officially requires more than 28 GB, so 24 GB is officially unsupported there, even though about 21.5 GB was measured.
Official int4 repos: openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5-awq (AWQ gemm, 4-bit, group 128, about 11 GB) and openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5-GPTQ (W4A16, about 11 GB per its card, loaded with auto-gptq and device_map="auto"). There is no openbmb MiniCPM-o-4_5-int4 (bitsandbytes) repo. No official doc shows AWQ or GPTQ running full-duplex streaming, so that is UNCONFIRMED.

PIP PINS FOR 4.5. The GitHub guide gives:
pip install "transformers==4.51.0" accelerate "torch>=2.3.0,<=2.8.0" "torchaudio<=2.8.0" "minicpmo-utils[all]>=1.0.5"
The [all] extra is needed for TTS and streaming. Tested on Python 3.10.
- The HF card, changed 2026-10-16, caps it at "minicpmo-utils[all]>=1.0.5,<=1.0.6". minicpmo-utils 1.0.7 appeared on PyPI 3 minutes later. The reason for the cap is not stated.
- What minicpmo-utils pulls in: pillow==10.4.0, librosa==0.9.0, decord==0.6.0 and moviepy==2.1.2. The tts extra adds transformers>=4.51.0,<4.53.0, onnxruntime>=1.18.0,<=1.21.0, einops==0.8.1 and soundfile==0.12.1.
- The Demo requirements.txt pins transformers==4.51.0 and accelerate==1.12.0. It also requires librosa>=0.10.2: a comment says 0.9.x crashes on import with new setuptools. That conflicts with minicpmo-utils' librosa==0.9.0 pin. The Dockerfile works around this by installing minicpmo-utils first. The Dockerfile itself uses python:3.12-slim-bookworm and torch==2.8.0 / torchaudio==2.8.0 from the cu128 index.
- flash-attn is optional. sdpa is the default in the examples, and the Whisper audio module always uses sdpa. The Demo's install.sh lists flash-attn ">=2.7.1,<=2.8.2" as "officially recommended", but that step is commented out and labelled "Not Recommended".
- vector-quantize-pytorch and vocos are NOT used by 4.5. They appear only in requirements_o2.6.txt (1.18.5 and 0.1.0). The 4.5 TTS uses stepaudio2.Token2wav, which comes from minicpmo-utils[all].

PORTS (from the Demo). Gateway 8006 over HTTPS; the browser mic and camera need HTTPS. Internal registry on 8007, worker on 22400, backend on 22500. The cookbook's standalone llama-omni-server example uses 28099. That server defaults to HTTPS (LLAMA_OPENSSL=ON) and exits right away if it has no certificate. The WebRTC_Demo needs LiveKit 7880, 7891→7881/tcp, 7882/udp and 50000-50100/udp, plus 3000, 8025 and 9060.

summary:
I read the Runpod docs as raw markdown (docs.runpod.io/<path>.md), plus the pricing page HTML and the public GraphQL API. All results are recorded in the facts.

1. **Templates.** Template fields come from /pods/templates/manage-templates and the REST TemplateCreateInput schema: imageName, containerRegistryAuthId, dockerStartCmd, dockerEntrypoint, containerDiskInGb (default 50), volumeInGb (default 20), volumeMountPath (default /workspace), ports as "8888/http" or "22/tcp", env, secrets written as {{ RUNPOD_SECRET_name }}. The proxy URL is https://<podId>-<port>.proxy.runpod.net, with at most 10 HTTP ports. It is HTTPS only and has a 100 s Cloudflare timeout that returns a 524. The docs do not confirm that the proxy carries WebSockets; they suggest TCP exposure for persistent connections. Also covered: SSH requirements, the env vars Runpod injects (RUNPOD_POD_ID, RUNPOD_TCP_PORT_22, PUBLIC_KEY and others), and that Pods have no Docker-in-Docker, Docker Compose or UDP.

2. **Storage.** Container disk is lost on stop. The volume disk keeps /workspace until the Pod is terminated. A network volume lives on its own, replaces /workspace, is Secure Cloud only and must be attached when the Pod is created. Prices per GB-month:
   - Container disk: $0.10 while running, nothing when stopped.
   - Volume disk: $0.10 running, $0.20 stopped.
   - Network volume: $0.07 under 1 TB and $0.05 over, running or stopped. High-performance is $0.14 on the pricing page.

3. **S3 API.** The facts list 15 datacenters with their exact endpoint URLs. The access key is the user_... ID and the secret is rps_.... Multipart upload and ListObjectsV2 are supported. PutObject takes files under 500 MB, parts can be at most 500 MB and the largest object is 4 TB. Presigned URLs, DeleteObjects, versioning and ACLs are not supported. It works without a running Pod. The docs say nothing about symlinks.

4. **Stopping and terminating.** Commands are listed for the console, runpodctl, REST v1 and v2, and GraphQL (podStop, podTerminate). Status values: desiredStatus RUNNING, EXITED or TERMINATED; the v2 API adds PROVISIONING, STARTING and ERROR; runpodctl reports runtimeStatus. After a stop, volume disk and network volume storage keep billing.

5. **GPU prices.** The pricing page was updated 2026-10-08. Secure / Community per hour:
   - RTX A6000: $0.59 / $0.33
   - A40: $0.59 / $0.35 (the API says Community is not offered)
   - L40S: $1.09 / $0.79
   - RTX 6000 Ada: $0.99 / $0.74
   - L40: $0.82 / $0.69
   - RTX 3090: $0.50 / $0.22
   - RTX 4090: $0.89 / $0.34

   The public GraphQL API returns the same numbers. The docs do not say which S3-enabled datacenters have 48 GB GPUs, so I took a live, unconfirmed snapshot from the GraphQL dataCenters query. It shows 48 GB cards in US-KS-2, US-MO-1, US-IL-1, US-NC-1, US-CA-2, US-WA-1, EU-RO-1 and US-NE-1. The same API reports storageSupport=false for US-GA-2, US-MD-1 and US-MO-2, even though the docs list them as S3 datacenters.

summary:
Research into the GitHub Actions to GHCR build path for a large CUDA image (MiniCPM-o 4.5 on Runpod), as of 2026-10-22. Sources were read directly: the GitHub REST API (via curl, then the read-only `gh api` once the unauthenticated rate limit ran out), the docker/docs source at commit 4d64a8e4f0a59967fc0b391120d54a90e9ccb60d (main on 2026-10-22T03:43:47Z, the source of docs.docker.com), the action READMEs on raw.githubusercontent.com, and GitHub Docs through docs.github.com/api/article/body?pathname=... (the same content as the rendered pages).

Current actions:
- docker/setup-buildx-action@v4: latest v4.4.1, f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069
- docker/login-action@v4: latest v4.6.0, dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f
- docker/build-push-action@v7: latest v7.4.0, c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc
- docker/metadata-action@v6: latest v6.2.0, dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302
- actions/checkout@v7: latest v7.0.1, 3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
- docker/setup-qemu-action@v4: latest v4.4.0, 99012661954931238ded8c8b007157a8430204e1

In every case the moving major tag currently points at the same commit as the latest release. All four Docker action majors switched to Node 24, which needs Actions Runner v2.327.1 or later.

Pushing to GHCR:
- Log in with docker/login-action, using registry: ghcr.io, username: ${{ github.actor }} and password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}.
- Job permissions: contents: read and packages: write. Add attestations: write and id-token: write only if you use actions/attest@v4.
- Once you declare any permission, every permission you leave out is set to none.
- The digest is the `digest` output of build-push-action, read as ${{ steps.<id>.outputs.digest }}. Other outputs are `imageid` and `metadata`.

Cache:
- Use cache-from: type=gha and cache-to: type=gha,mode=max.
- GitHub's default cache limit is 10 GB per repository, and entries not accessed for 7 days are evicted. The limit can now be raised (up to 10 TB on user-owned repos), and anything above 10 GB is billed.
- Defaults for the gha backend: scope `buildkit` and timeout 10m.
- Some triggers (issue_comment, pull_request_target, and pull_request with types: [closed]) get read-only cache access, so cache-to fails there. Use `ignore-error=true` or populate the cache from a `push` workflow.

Secrets:
- Never pass secrets as ARG or ENV; they stay in the final image.
- Public repos get mode=max provenance by default, which records build-arg values.
- Use the `secrets` / `secret-envs` / `secret-files` inputs together with `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=...[,env=...|,target=...]` in the Dockerfile. The secret is mounted at /run/secrets/<id> only for that one instruction.

GHCR limits and billing:
- Each layer can be at most 10 GB, and uploads time out after 10 minutes. This matters if model weights are baked into the image.
- GHCR image storage and bandwidth are currently free, with at least one month's notice before that changes. Public packages are free in general.
- The free plan's private Packages quota (500MB storage, 1GB/month transfer, storage shared with Actions artifacts) applies to other registries, not to GHCR while it stays free.

GHCR visibility (GitHub's docs contradict each other):
- Three pages say a package's first publish is private by default, and one says a linked package inherits access permissions "but not the visibility".
- The page on publishing from workflows says a package created by a workflow with GITHUB_TOKEN "inherits the visibility and permissions model of the repository".
- Plan to check after the first push and make the package Public by hand if needed. That change is irreversible.
- Public GHCR packages can be pulled anonymously.

Runners:
- ubuntu-24.04 on a public repo: 4 CPU, 16 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD, free and unlimited.
- ubuntu-24.04 on a private repo: 2 CPU, 8 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD.
- A job can run at most 6 hours (timeout-minutes defaults to 360). A workflow run can last at most 35 days.
- A runner-images contributor says the guaranteed free disk is 14 GB. Their July 2026 `df -h` showed a 72G root with 16G free and no separate /mnt disk.
- `ubuntu-latest` moves to 26.04 between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19, so pin `ubuntu-24.04`.
- The current 24.04 image (20261012.334.1) ships Docker 28.0.4 and Buildx 0.38.0.

Freeing disk for CUDA images:
- Delete /usr/local/lib/android, /usr/share/dotnet, /opt/ghc, /usr/local/.ghcup and $AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY, then run `docker image prune -af` and purge apt packages.
- The third-party jlumbroso/free-disk-space v2.0.0 (ceedf095f4ec1a097402bc6bd80831f2e1a6fde6, released 2026-09-17) does this. It removes android, dotnet, haskell, large-packages and docker-images by default; preinstalled-runtimes and swap-storage are off by default.
- easimon/maximize-build-space (last release v10, 2023-12-07) relies on /mnt. The `df -h` above shows no separate /mnt disk, so it may not work on today's images (unconfirmed).

Two caveats on examples:
- GitHub's own GHCR tutorial pins outdated action SHAs; f4ef78c0 is login-action v2.1.0 and 3b5e8027 is build-push-action v4.0.0. Use the SHAs above instead.
- The Docker docs and the build-push-action README still show actions/checkout@v6, although v7.0.1 is the latest.

Majors released March 2026: build-push-action v7.0.0, login-action v4.0.0, setup-buildx-action v4.0.0 and metadata-action v6.0.0 all make Node 24 the default runtime, which requires Actions Runner v2.327.1 or later. build-push-action v7 also removed the deprecated DOCKER_BUILD_NO_SUMMARY and DOCKER_BUILD_EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS env vars.

The Docker docs' hugo.yaml version params at docker/docs@4d64a8e are: build_push_action_version v7, login_action_version v4, metadata_action_version v6, setup_buildx_action_version v4, setup_qemu_action_version v4, setup_docker_action_version v5, checkout_action_version v6, cache_action_version v5, github_builder_version v1 and buildkit_version 0.32.0. The docs still say checkout v6 even though v7 exists.

build-push-action outputs: `imageid` (Image ID), `digest` (Image digest), `metadata` (JSON build result metadata). Reference as ${{ steps.<id>.outputs.digest }}; GitHub's tutorial uses `id: push` and `subject-digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}` with actions/attest@v4.

Relevant inputs: context (default is the Git context, so file changes made in earlier steps are ignored unless you use actions/checkout with `context: .`), file, push, load, tags, labels, platforms, cache-from, cache-to, secrets, secret-envs, secret-files, provenance, sbom, shm-size, github-token (default ${{ github.token }}), build-args. Env DOCKER_BUILD_RECORD_UPLOAD (default true) uploads a .dockerbuild record artifact; set it to false to save artifact storage.

GitHub's official GHCR workflow uses: env REGISTRY: ghcr.io and IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}. The job has `permissions: { contents: read, packages: write, attestations: write, id-token: write }`. Login is docker/login-action with registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}, username: ${{ github.actor }}, password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}. Then a metadata-action step (id: meta, images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}), a build-push-action step (id: push, push: true, tags/labels from steps.meta.outputs), and actions/attest@v4 with subject-name, subject-digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }} and push-to-registry: true. attestations and id-token are only needed for the attest step.

The GitHub tutorial pins outdated action SHAs. docker/login-action f4ef78c080cd8ba55a85445d5b36e214a81df20a = v2.1.0 and docker/build-push-action 3b5e8027fcad23fda98b2e3ac259d8d67585f671 = v4.0.0. The other pinned SHAs (65b78e6e..., 9ec57ed1..., f2a1d5e9...) were not in each repo's newest 100 tags, so they are also old. Do not copy these pins.

The docker/login-action README GHCR example is `uses: docker/login-action@v4` with registry: ghcr.io, username: ${{ github.actor }}, password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}. The Docker docs multi-registry example uses username: ${{ github.repository_owner }} instead.
If you specify the access for any permission, all permissions you leave out are set to `none`. `packages: write` lets an action upload and publish packages.

Publishing from a workflow with GITHUB_TOKEN links the package to the workflow's repo automatically. GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push if a package of the same name was already pushed to that namespace without being connected to the repo. GitHub recommends adding the label org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.
GHCR troubleshooting limits: 10 GB maximum per layer, and a 10-minute timeout for uploads. Model weights baked into an image must be split into layers under 10 GB, or downloaded at runtime instead.

The Container registry page says: 'When you first publish a package, the default visibility is private.' The access-control page says a package linked to a repo 'automatically inherits the access permissions (but not the visibility) of the linked repository'. It also says: 'Once you make a package public, you cannot make it private again.'

This page contradicts the visibility statements above: 'by default if a workflow creates a package using the GITHUB_TOKEN, then: The package inherits the visibility and permissions model of the repository where the workflow is run.' Repository admins become admins of the package.
In the Container registry, public packages can be pulled anonymously without authenticating.

GitHub Packages usage is free for public packages, and data transferred in is free. The private-package quota is shared with Actions artifacts: GitHub Free 500MB storage and 1GB transfer per month, Pro 2GB/10GB, Free for orgs 500MB/1GB, Team 2GB/10GB, Enterprise Cloud 50GB/100GB. Container registry storage and bandwidth are 'currently free', with at least one month's notice before any change. Downloads by Actions using GITHUB_TOKEN are free. With no payment method on file, usage is blocked once the quota is used up. The legacy managing-billing URL serves the same content as /en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-packages.

Docker docs: use `cache-from: type=gha` and `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max`. Only GitHub Cache service API v2 is supported since April 15, 2025; minimums are Buildx >= v0.21.0 and BuildKit >= v0.20.0. With build-push-action, url and token are filled in automatically. Read-only cache events (issue_comment, pull_request_target, and pull_request types:[closed]) can fail with 'failed to reserve cache'. Keep cache-from, drop cache-to, or add `ignore-error=true`.

gha backend parameters: scope (default `buildkit`; each build overwrites the previous one's cache unless you set a distinct scope per image), mode (min|max, default min), ignore-error (default false), timeout (default 10m), ghtoken and repository. build-push-action sets ghtoken to GITHUB_TOKEN automatically to reduce cache API throttling. Rendered at https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/gha/

GitHub cache limits: entries not accessed in more than 7 days are removed. The default total is 10 GB per repository, evicted by last access date. Usage beyond 10 GB is billed. User-owned repos can configure up to 10 TB, and only users with a payment method on file can opt in. Rate limits: 200 uploads/min, 1500 downloads/min, 400 deletes/min per repo. If a budget is exceeded, the cache becomes read-only.
Actions storage limits table: GitHub Free has 500 MB artifact storage, 2,000 minutes per month (private repos) and 10 GB cache storage per repository. GitHub Support cannot increase storage limits.
The new workflow/job key `cache-mode` (read, write, write-only, none) controls cache access. If omitted, a trigger-based default applies.
Build args and environment variables 'persist in the final image', so use secret mounts or SSH mounts instead.

Three build-push-action inputs map to Buildx options. `secrets: MY_SECRET=value` becomes --secret id=MY_SECRET,src=<temp-file>. `secret-envs: MY_SECRET=MY_ENV_VAR` becomes --secret id=MY_SECRET,env=MY_ENV_VAR. `secret-files: MY_SECRET=./secret.txt` becomes --secret id=MY_SECRET,src=./secret.txt. In the Dockerfile, `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=MY_SECRET` mounts the secret at /run/secrets/MY_SECRET; add `env=VAR` to expose it as an environment variable or `target=` to change the path. Multi-line values must be quoted. Rendered at https://docs.docker.com/build/ci/github-actions/secrets/

build-push-action adds provenance by default: mode=max for public repos and mode=min for private repos. No provenance is added with load: true or the docker exporter. Warning: in public repos the default provenance contains build-arg values, so secrets passed as build args are exposed. SBOM is opt-in with `sbom: true`. Rendered at https://docs.docker.com/build/ci/github-actions/attestations/

Use `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64` with setup-qemu and setup-buildx. The docker/github-builder reusable workflow (build.yml, docs param v1; latest release v1.18.1 on 2026-10-21) can run one platform per runner. Its default runner mapping sends Linux Arm to ubuntu-24.04-arm and everything else to ubuntu-24.04. A Runpod CUDA image only needs linux/amd64.

setup-buildx-action's default driver is `docker-container`. Other inputs: version (e.g. `latest`), driver-opts, buildkitd-flags, buildkitd-config-inline, cache-binary (default true), cleanup (default true).

Standard runners for public repos: ubuntu-latest / ubuntu-24.04 / ubuntu-22.04 / ubuntu-26.04 have 4 CPU, 16 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD, x64. Use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited on public repositories. ubuntu-24.04-arm has the same 4 CPU / 16 GB / 14 GB. ubuntu-slim has 1 CPU, 5 GB RAM, 14 GB, and a 15-minute job timeout.

Standard runners for private repos: ubuntu-latest / ubuntu-24.04 have 2 CPU, 8 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD, x64. These runners use the account's free minutes (Free plan: 2,000/month) and are then billed per minute.

GitHub-hosted runners: 6 hours of execution time per job, after which the job is terminated and fails. A workflow run can last at most 35 days. Self-hosted jobs can run up to 5 days. `jobs.<job_id>.timeout-minutes` defaults to 360. Free plan: 20 concurrent jobs.

A runner-images contributor (2026-07-16) said: 'the guaranteed free disk space for Ubuntu runners is 14 GB'. Their df -h on image 20260714.240.1 showed /dev/root at 72G size, 57G used, 16G available, with no separate /mnt mount. VMs of different sizes can give more space, which makes disk errors flaky, so design for 14 GB.

The Ubuntu 24.04 runner image is 20261012.334.1 (OS 24.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure) with Docker Client/Server 28.0.4, Docker-Buildx 0.38.0 and Docker Compose 2.38.2. Large preinstalled tools: Android SDK (ANDROID_HOME=/usr/local/lib/android/sdk), .NET SDKs 8/9/10, GHC 9.14.1 with GHCup, Miniconda at /usr/share/miniconda, CodeQL bundle, Swift 6.4, Julia.
`ubuntu-latest` will switch to Ubuntu 26.04. The rollout begins October 19, 2026 and is planned to finish by November 19, 2026. Pin `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` for reproducibility.

Third-party action jlumbroso/free-disk-space v2.0.0 (released 2026-09-17, commit ceedf095f4ec1a097402bc6bd80831f2e1a6fde6). Inputs and defaults: android true (rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android), dotnet true (rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet), haskell true (rm -rf /opt/ghc /usr/local/.ghcup), large-packages true (apt remove of llvm, php, mongodb, mysql, azure-cli, chrome, firefox, powershell, mono, google-cloud-cli), docker-images true (docker image prune --all --force), preinstalled-runtimes false (removes $AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY; replaces the deprecated tool-cache input), swap-storage false (swapoff and rm /mnt/swapfile).

easimon/maximize-build-space: latest release v10 (2023-12-07), last push 2025-03-28. It relies on combining root and /mnt with LVM. The July 2026 df showed no /mnt disk, so this may not work on current images.

To pass a single-platform image between jobs without a registry, use outputs: type=docker,dest=${{ runner.temp }}/myimage.tar with upload-artifact and download-artifact, then `docker load`. This counts against artifact storage (500 MB on the Free plan), so it is impractical for multi-GB CUDA images.

unconfirmed: Which GHCR visibility applies to a package first published from a public repo's workflow with GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub Docs contradict each other (default private and 'not the visibility' on one side, 'inherits the visibility ... of the repository' on the other). Check after the first push with an anonymous `docker pull`, and set the package to Public by hand if needed; that change is irreversible.

Per-GB overage prices for GitHub Packages and for Actions cache storage above 10 GB. The billing pages point to the pricing calculator and give no rate. This does not matter for GHCR while it is 'currently free'.

Whether current ubuntu-24.04 VMs still have a separate /mnt temp disk. The July 2026 df showed none, so moving Docker's data-root or BuildKit state to /mnt, or using easimon/maximize-build-space, may not work.

Exact free space reclaimed by each cleanup step on image 20261012.334.1. Third-party reports say roughly 15-25 GB in total, with Android about 8.9G and .NET about 1.6G, but these figures are not official. Measure with `df -h` before and after.
Whether the gha cache with mode=max for a multi-GB CUDA image stays within the 10 GB repository default without thrashing. That depends on the image's layer sizes, which were not measured.
